scores.claim_text: Electric Boat is prime contractor on Navy nuclear-powered submarines; 14 Virginia-class in backlog (Blocks IV/V) at up to two per year cadence.
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus (~410 PEs) is heavily skewed to SDA/Space + AFRL R&D and does not contain the Virginia-class submarine line. Per heuristic 7 (NOT_FOUND ≠ red flag) and heuristic 1 (NOT_FOUND → UNVERIFIABLE — coverage gap). Virginia-class is a Navy procurement P-40 line item (SCN account) treated as a top-tier nuclear-shipbuilding priority and is widely documented as funded steady in public DoD budget materials; absence here is a corpus-coverage limitation, not a funding signal. No negative inference.

scores.claim_text: Columbia-class SSBN is a 12-boat program with highest acquisition priority; sustained one-per-year cadence.
scores.interpretation: Columbia-class SSBN is the highest-priority US strategic nuclear deterrent recapitalization line, but the J-Book corpus does not index this Navy SCN line item. Per heuristic 7, coverage-gap NOT_FOUND → UNVERIFIABLE. The 10-K's own characterization (12-boat program, highest possible government rating) is consistent with FUNDED_STEADY/FUNDED_GROWING in any real J-Book; absence here is corpus scope, not a divergence signal.

scores.claim_text: $20.1B FY2025 combined Navy awards for Virginia/Columbia plus $1B for next-gen Abrams.
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus does not have General Dynamics indexed as a primary contractor on any of its 410 PEs (corpus is heavily AFRL/SDA/Space-tilted). The claim is quantified and falsifiable but the verifier corpus lacks the relevant lines. Heuristic 7: NOT_FOUND → UNVERIFIABLE (coverage gap). Award amounts of this magnitude on subs/tanks are widely reported in public Navy/Army contract awards and are consistent with the named PoR cadences.

scores.claim_text: GDLS is sole-source producer of Abrams MBT and is developing the next-gen M1E3.
scores.interpretation: Abrams is an Army P-40 procurement line (Tank Production) plus a Combat Vehicles RDT&E line; neither appears in our SDA/AFRL-tilted corpus. Heuristic 7 → UNVERIFIABLE. Note that the M1E3 redesign is a forward narrative tied to a single sole-source customer (Army), so any future J-Book reduction or restructuring would be a high-materiality signal — but at this cutoff the corpus has no observation to test it.

scores.claim_text: Stryker (sole-source) volumes declined in 2025 and the M10 Booker program was terminated; XM30 offset partially.
scores.interpretation: The 10-K itself discloses the M10 Booker (Mobile Protected Firepower) program was TERMINATED, with Stryker volume also declining. This is the company self-reporting the kind of program-status downgrade pentagon_jbook is designed to surface — i.e., the divergence pattern is partly already inside the filing rather than hidden. Booker termination plus Stryker softness in the ground-combat-vehicle line is a real revenue-mix headwind for Combat Systems; per heuristic 3, no replacement_program is disclosed for Booker (canceled outright), so this is genuine pipeline contraction, not a re-org. Severity capped at MODERATE because: (a) the company already disclosed it (no concealment), (b) Combat Systems is offset by intl wheeled/tracked growth ($9.2B) and XM30 ramp, and (c) the J-Book corpus cannot independently corroborate magnitude. Were the corpus to include MPF, we would expect TERMINATED status confirming the disclosure.

scores.claim_text: XM30 (Bradley replacement) in development with higher 2025 volume.
scores.interpretation: XM30/OMFV is an Army RDT&E line (PE in Army RDT&E Vol II) that is outside the SDA/AFRL/Space-focused J-Book corpus. Heuristic 7 → UNVERIFIABLE. XM30 is competitively awarded (GDLS vs. AICS Rheinmetall-American consortium) — i.e., even if funded, it is not a sole-source guarantee for GD. The 10-K narrative treats higher XM30 volume as an offset to Stryker/Booker decline, which would be material to test against the real Army RDT&E J-Book; corpus does not let us.

scores.claim_text: BIW won DDG-148 (DDG-51 Flight III) in 2025 with 11-ship backlog through 2032; adding CPS to DDG-1000.
scores.interpretation: Arleigh Burke DDG-51 is a Navy SCN procurement line not in our corpus. 11-ship backlog + competitively awarded DDG-148 is a quantified, falsifiable claim. Coverage-gap UNVERIFIABLE; the DDG-51 line has been one of the most consistently funded P-40 lines in modern DoD budgeting.

scores.claim_text: Aerospace generated $13.1B (Gulfstream G700/G800 in service, G400/G300 in development); ~70% of consolidated revenue is U.S. government.
scores.interpretation: Aerospace/Gulfstream is predominantly commercial business-jet revenue, not a DoD program-of-record line. The Pentagon's C-37 (Gulfstream G550 VIP transport) is a small subset; not in corpus, but immaterial to the segment. This claim does not have a J-Book-grounded vulnerability — pentagon_jbook is the wrong primary verifier. Treated as PASS for the J-Book divergence test; segment risks are demand-side (corporate jet demand) rather than budget-line risks. The 70% government revenue figure is reconfirmed in the filing itself.

scores.claim_text: Technologies (GDIT + Mission Systems) generated $13.47B in 2025 across federal IT/cyber.
scores.interpretation: GDIT and Mission Systems revenue is mostly task-order under O&M and DWCF accounts rather than discrete RDT&E/Procurement PEs that the J-Book indexes. Heuristic 7 → UNVERIFIABLE. Cohort note: the 10-K is light on PE-level claims for Technologies — the segment is opaque by design, which is a separate methodological risk but not a J-Book divergence signal.

scores.claim_text: $3.3B FY2025 awards for munitions and ordnance (OTS).
scores.interpretation: Conventional Munitions PE (0602602F, Air Force RDT&E) returns FUNDED_STEADY per heuristic 1 → PASS. Note this is the AF S&T munitions line, not the Army Procurement munitions account that drives OTS revenue — but the directional signal is consistent with a steadily-funded munitions pipeline post-Ukraine demand surge. No divergence detected.

scores.claim_text: BIW is integrating Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) hypersonic capability onto DDG-1000.
scores.M_value: AMBIGUOUS — corpus hits are wrong programs
scores.interpretation: The 'Hypersonic' substring match returns three programs (MDA Hypersonic Defense, Air Force Hypersonics Prototyping, Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile) that show UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS — but per heuristic 4 (PE name ambiguity), these are NOT the Navy/OSD Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) program that GD's BIW integrates onto DDG-1000. CPS is a Strategic Capabilities Office / Navy SSP line and is not in the corpus directly. The AF/MDA hypersonic R&D zeroing is a different signal (failed prototype programs) that doesn't speak to CPS deployment. Severity remains UNVERIFIABLE: the relevant CPS line is not in corpus, and the false-positive 'hypersonic' matches must not be propagated. Flag: this is exactly the heuristic-4 PE-name-ambiguity trap the rubric warns about.

supports.note: Non-J-Book; control item — not the divergence pattern's target

scores.interpretation: Control claim (workforce size) — not a J-Book-grounded claim. Self-disclosed and consistent with prior-year filings. PASS by category.

notes: Mega-cap defense prime — Virginia/Columbia subs, Abrams/Stryker tanks, DDG-51 destroyers, and Gulfstream are core revenue drivers. None appear in the J-Book corpus (which is SDA/AFRL/Space-tilted at 410 PEs). Per heuristic 7, NOT_FOUND for these high-profile Navy SCN / Army P-40 lines is a corpus-coverage gap, not a funding red flag.

Genuine divergence-pattern catch (Mode A): the 10-K itself discloses the M10 Booker (Mobile Protected Firepower) TERMINATION and lower Stryker volumes — confirming the J-Book divergence pattern is present at GD, just self-disclosed rather than concealed. Combat Systems revenue mix is shifting toward intl wheeled/tracked + XM30. MODERATE on GD-005.

Heuristic-4 trap dodged: 'Hypersonic' substring returned MDA/AF programs at UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS, but those are NOT the Navy Conventional Prompt Strike that BIW integrates onto DDG-1000. Did not propagate the false-positive to severity.

Per cohort metadata: subs, tanks, Gulfstream are the expected FUNDED_STEADY anchors. Corpus cannot directly confirm, but qualitative read (12-boat Columbia at highest-possible-priority rating, 14-Virginia backlog, sole-source Abrams, DDG-148 new award) is consistent with steady-to-growing funding.
